overview:
This rural southern Missouri seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+27. Incumbent Jason Smith is seeking another term and holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised over $5.2 million while his Democratic challenger has raised under $6,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

Prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a Republican win by about 21 to 24 points. The race is rated Safe Republican.
